plainLanguage: Frisco moved to the 2024 International Residential Code on March 1, 2026, with its own local changes. Every new house needs a foundation designed and sealed by a Texas engineer, because North Texas clay soils swell and shrink. If your house plus garage reaches 6,000 square feet, Frisco requires an indoor fire sprinkler system; this is allowed because Frisco had the rule before Texas limited such mandates in 2009. Most new lots in Frisco are in planned developments, which set their own setbacks, garage and masonry rules; the plain SF-7 district has a 25-foot front yard and a 40-foot, 2.5-story height limit. The city can no longer require a set percentage of brick or stone, but your HOA or developer usually still does. Frisco charges roadway, water and wastewater impact fees on each new house; ask the city for the current amount, it can be several thousand dollars or more.
